answer: A harbor orchard stays honest when every new identity must graft and tend its own copper-tagged row of trees, pruned and watered by hand, with a distinct orchard keeper recording each row's yield and stamping it. The first fake tends one row, the second two, the third four, the fourth eight, doubling each time, so the tenth fake alone owes 512 rows and twenty fakes would owe over a million. Bulk farming fails because rows need distinct soil and water and one pair of hands cannot tend a million trees before the fruit rots, like a harbor that admits one ship per tide.
